title: On convexity and efficiency in semantic systems

cost.compute_notes: arXiv PDF (11 pp incl. appendices) read in full via PyMuPDF. Supplementary materials are behind a tinyurl to an interactive app; no data or code located. Nothing re-run here; the quantitative cross-check is the null ladder in zaslavsky2018-color-naming-ib (same model, same WCS data).

triggers: is convexity the same as efficiency for semantic categories
are convex color categories automatically efficient
convexity versus information bottleneck explanation of semantic typology
how to sample convex partitions for a null model

claims.statement: Convexity and IB-efficiency do not entail each other: an IB-optimal system can be non-convex (Theorem 1, angle domain with direction-indifferent similarity) and for any convex system there is a need distribution under which it is non-informative while another convex system is maximally informative (Theorem 2).
claims.scope: Constructive proofs on a one-dimensional angle domain; the Theorem 2 prior is built for the system it defeats.

our_assessment.why: The proofs are short and correct as I read them. Their scope is existential: they show the properties CAN come apart, under constructed priors, not how far apart they are in the colour domain under the priors actually used there. The authors note that the Theorem 2 world makes the system trivially efficient in IB terms and fall back on the RKK notion for the inefficiency.

claims.statement: A large number of perfectly convex colour systems are highly inefficient (971,525 Voronoi systems, k = 3-17), so convexity is too permissive.
claims.scope: Systems generated by (1) a greedy exemplar-swap search from random starts, all states along 20 trajectories per k recorded, and (2) a deterministic agglomerative merge that at each step keeps the LOWEST-accuracy merge.

our_assessment.why: As an existence claim, adversarial search is exactly the right tool and the claim stands. As a picture of convex systems in general -- how Figure 3a invites reading -- it is not: the sample is built to be inefficient. Random convex partitions under the same model are typically far closer to the bound (median eps 0.29 against 1.93 for random partitions and 0.19 for real mode maps; zaslavsky2018-color-naming-ib#c1). And the generator is described two ways: the text says the greedy search minimises the IB accuracy term by replacing exemplars with colours that yield lower accuracy, while Algorithm 1 swaps only when Acc(E_cand) - Acc(E) > 0, i.e. when accuracy RISES. One of the two is a typo; which one changes what the gray cloud in Figure 3a is.

claims.statement: Efficiency discriminates attested colour systems from their 39 hue rotations far better than convexity: 93% of attested systems are more efficient than all rotations vs 13% more convex; the efficiency-based classifier is at ceiling (ROC AUC) and convexity adds negligible likelihood (LRT chi2 42.9 for removing efficiency's partner vs 7445.4 for removing efficiency).
claims.scope: WCS, hard partitions for convexity, soft encoders for efficiency; logistic classifiers on pairwise differences, 5-fold CV.

quantities.name: share_languages_beating_all_hue_rotations
quantities.baseline: efficiency (eps); convexity advantage over all rotations: 13%

our_assessment.why: The numbers are plausible and the 93% matches my reproduction of the 2018 paper (94%). The inference that efficiency explains more than convexity does not follow from this comparison: a hue rotation of a convex system is itself (approximately) convex, so convexity CANNOT separate a system from its rotations by construction, and the test measures alignment with hue and with the need distribution. The question how much of the efficiency of attested systems convexity alone delivers needs random convex systems as the comparison, and there the answer is most of it (~85%) with a real residual (~5 points) for actual languages.

relations.why: Same model and data, second author is the 2018 first author: asks whether the 2018 efficiency result is just convexity.
Both use hue rotations as THE hypothetical alternative; rotations preserve convexity, size and geometry, so neither paper's control can measure what a minimal structural constraint alone buys.

open_questions: Which is right for Algorithm 1 -- minimise or maximise accuracy? Ask the authors, or rerun from their SM if code appears.
Report the efficiency distribution of UNoptimised random convex systems beside the adversarial cloud; on our reanalysis it is median eps 0.29 (zaslavsky2018#c1).
